endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Organizations should follow applicable human subjects research requirements, and best practices such as informed consent and subject compensation, when implementing feedback activities.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Before detailing the baseline operational controls for Subdomain 4.1: Responsible AI Lifecycle Management and Use of health AI solutions, organizations should first understand how AI solutions enter the organization, referred to as the ingestion modality.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Is an IRB submission necessary for research involving the solution’s use on human participants?

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: This should be subject to informed consent and approval by ethics committees to ensure an appropriate balance between the benefits of non-discrimination and the risks of reidentification.

endorsements.title: Ethical framework for artificial intelligence in healthcare research: A path to integrity
endorsements.quote: Implementing ethical review processes specifically tailored to AI projects in healthcare research, akin to traditional human subjects’ research oversight; and (2) Establishing ethics committees or boards with expertise to evaluate AI projects, focusing on the potential risks, benefits, and ethical considerations.

endorsements.title: Toward real-world deployment of machine learning for health care: External validation, continual monitoring, and randomized clinical trials
endorsements.quote: Assuming that an ML tool demonstrates accurate prospective diagnostic capabilities in the target setting, its developers should pursue approval for further RCTs from administrative ethics committees.

endorsements.title: Navigating the potential and pitfalls of large language models in patient-centered medication guidance and self-decision support
endorsements.quote: Looking forward, establishing medical AI ethical review boards, similar to institutional review boards for clinical research, could provide structured oversight of LLM implementation.

endorsements.title: Utilizing large language models for gastroenterology research: a conceptual framework
endorsements.quote: Approval from the ethics committee or institutional review board must be secured to ensure compliance with ethical standards.

endorsements.title: Expert Consensus Best Practices for the Safe, Ethical, and Effective Design and Implementation of Artificially Intelligent Conversational Agent (i.e., Chatbot/Virtual Human) Systems in Health Care Applications
endorsements.quote: As with all areas of human research, institutional review boards (IRBs) are essential in overseeing research involving AICA applications in health care and wellness, ensuring human subject protection.

endorsements.title: Health Equity Considerations in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
endorsements.quote: As AI tools are increasingly integrated into clinical research and care delivery, institutional review boards must be equipped to assess issues related to algorithmic bias, data privacy, and participant protections.

endorsements.title: Prioritizing human-AI collaboration in healthcare: the TRIAD framework for trustworthy governance, real-world, and integrated adaptive deployment
endorsements.quote: In health systems, this maps to ethics/institutional review board (IRB) oversight, de-identification and privacy impact work, and conformance to established reporting and safety frameworks.

endorsements.title: Governing Patient-Facing AI-Generated Video in Digital Health: A Risk-and-Ethics Matrix for Deployment, Monitoring, and Change Control
endorsements.quote: Under IRB-approved protocols, a psychotherapist offers a time-bounded intervention in which a synthetic likeness of a deceased relative delivers scripted messages to facilitate goodbye rituals.

endorsements.title: The Real "Catch" in Clinical Automation: Rethinking Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare Workflows
endorsements.quote: Hospitals must treat silent deployments under the same ethical frameworks as clinical trials, utilizing them for operational metrics rather than high-acuity diagnostics, backed by legally binding data-processing agreements that prevent vendors from using ward data to train external commercial models.

endorsements.title: The AI-Driven Healthcare Value Framework-Rethinking Traditional Care Models in the Age of Automation
endorsements.quote: Relevant bioethics frameworks and IRB processes should also inform this governance layer, particularly for AI research involving consent, privacy, bias mitigation, data security, and algorithmic transparency.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether consulting an IRB or ethics committee before an AI pilot prevents unapproved research on patients, and no study documents how often that hazard occurs. The recommendation rests on 14 endorsing sources, mostly commentaries and consensus frameworks, that extend long-standing human subjects research norms to AI.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. The support comes from frameworks and commentaries that state expert opinion. Under GRADE conventions, expert opinion does not count as evidence of effect, so certainty that IRB consultation reduces unapproved research through AI pilots cannot be rated.

NIST AI 600-1 directs organizations to follow applicable human subjects research requirements, including informed consent, when running feedback activities. The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide asks whether an IRB submission is needed. These sources restate existing research obligations and do not report whether consultation changes compliance in practice.

One endorsing commentary on health equity states that IRBs must be equipped to assess algorithmic bias, data privacy, and participant protections. No supplied study examines whether IRB review of AI pilots addresses risks specific to Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that measure how often AI pilots proceed without an IRB determination, and whether a required pre-pilot consultation step changes that rate, the time to launch, or the rate of consent and oversight problems. Comparative work across health systems with and without formal AI intake review could supply direct evidence.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these patients have no evidence showing whether IRB review of AI pilots protects them or whether review processes account for consent and language barriers they face.
